content.text: The text surveys Byzantine, Neo-Byzantine, Armenian, Russian, and Italian medieval architecture. It praises Constantinople’s Hagia Sophia as an exceptionally beautiful and technically innovative church, emphasizing its domes, pendentives, mosaics, proportions, and influence. Later Byzantine architecture became smaller and less ambitious, while Armenian churches were modest but notable for elegant details and possible links to Eastern, Irish, Indian, and Russian traditions. Russian architecture is described as derivative Byzantine work shaped by Tartar domes, with St. Basil’s as its most distinctive example. The discussion then turns to Italian basilicas, Romanesque, Byzantine-Romanesque, Lombard, and Gothic styles, comparing churches, baptisteries, towers, domes, façades, decoration, and construction. It repeatedly contrasts Italian ornamental richness with Northern Gothic structural grandeur. Sandra went back to the bedroom.
